Declare a function parameter named `x_client_version` and annotate it with `Header()`. By default, `Header` will convert the parameter names characters from underscore (`_`) to hyphen (`-`) to extract and document the headers.[1] Also, HTTP headers are case-insensitive, so, you can declare them with standard Python style (also known as "snake_case").[1]

```python
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, Header

app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/items/")
async def read_items(x_client_version: Annotated[str | None, Header()] = None):
    return {"X-Client-Version": x_client_version}
```

Note that to declare headers, you need to use `Header`, because otherwise the parameters would be interpreted as query parameters.[5]

If the header may be sent more than once, you can define those cases using a list in the type declaration. You will receive all the values from the duplicate header as a Python `list`.[3]

More details: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/header-params/
